newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian share market weaker, Gardenia has rise.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian share market weaker, Gardenia has rise.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mostly lower on Monday as Friday's fall on Wall Street left its impact on the market, traders said.
The BUX index closed at 5,442.59 points, down 57.67.

"We felt the impact of the U.S. market," said Balazs Bathory of Creditanstalt Securities. "There isn't a selling pressure on the market but the buying side is rather weak, I think mainly due to the Friday's weakness of the U.S. market."
BUX futures settlement prices fell for all maturities, by between 63.00 and 85.50 points, with intraday clearings due to too rapid falls for March and December 1998 maturities.
The March maturity BUX fell 1,035 points, but the figure was due to human error, a BSE official said.
"BUX futures prices reflect uncertainty, everybody is waiting for the MOL and Richter issue, thus for an upward move," said Gyorgy Durucz of WestLB Investment.
"But there's uncertainty also because of the Dow," he said.
Spot share turnover totalled 2.14 billion forints, bolstered by block deals in MOL and OTP Bank, but traders said MOL generated good local demand as well.
MOL closed at 3,025 forints, down 35. OTP dipped five forints to 4,050.

While most stocks traded lower, a handful of shares bucked the trend, including plastics maker Pannonplast which hit a new record high of 8,730 forints before retreating to close unchanged at 8,700 forints.
The market's newcomer, curtain factory Gardenia began to trade amid rising prices. In a volume of 30,000 stocks, Gardenia closed at 1,765 forints, above its issue price of 1,465.

Analysts said the Dow's movements will remain a key driving factor for the Hungarian share market, which is the most sensitive in the region to changes on Wall Street, but the Dow's impact is likely to be reversed by earnings reports.
"If the results prove to be positive, the Hungarian market can become independent from international trends," said Rudi Voros, analyst at ICE Securities in London.
